subject: Clarify metering: billable token floors, ceilings, and streaming offsets
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@nobleretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nobleretail.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on metering: rounding, minimums, and streaming offsets

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Noble Retail liked the latency profile. Procurement has a few technical questions that will be gated in our SOW and PO:

1) Rounding: how do you round partial tokens? Do you round up to the next whole token, to a block (e.g., 50/100 tokens), or prorate?
2) Minimums / floors: is there a per-request minimum billable token floor (we use lots of short chat messages) and do committed monthly minima apply per month or per quarter?
3) Streaming: for websocket streaming, do you charge continuously by partial tokens or do you apply a prefix charge + chunked billing? Any example math would help.

I've attached a small sample of our traffic (short chat + some async batch inference) — we want to understand how charges map to our current bill.

Can you put together a short note we can include in our SOW? Also copying our procurement inbox so we can route a PO once terms are agreed.

Appreciate it,
Jordan Ellis
Procurement
Noble Retail

Attachment: NobleRetail_token_sample.csv (csv, 12 KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Questions on metering: rounding, minimums, and streaming offsets

Jordan — thanks for the clear note and the sample. High level answers below; I'll follow up with concrete contract language and a worked example attached.

Summary (short):
- Rounding: Hosted API billable units are counted as tokens. For negotiated customers we can apply rounding to the nearest 50 or 100 tokens for short-message workloads; default is per-token rounding (partial tokens rounded up to the next whole token).
- Per-request minimum/floor: We can offer a per-request floor (e.g., 25 tokens) as part of a short-message profile — otherwise no per-request floor beyond per-token billing. Monthly commit minima are evaluated per calendar month, but we can offer quarterly aggregation for certain commit tiers.
- Streaming: By default streaming uses continuous token accounting; however, for low-latency websocket streams we offer a "streaming offset" policy: a fixed prefix charge (e.g., 10 tokens) per call plus per-1k token rounding thereafter. That reduces noise for lots of short interactions.

I've attached a token_worksheet that maps your sample to (a) default per-token billing, (b) 50-token rounding, and (c) streaming-offset profile so you can compare monthly spend.

If Noble wants an alternate structure (fixed per-session charge + usage) we can surface that in the SOW and adjust discounts accordingly.

Next steps: I'll loop in Pricing for recommended discount/rounding trade-offs and Legal to draft SOW language you can attach to the PO.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on metering: rounding, minimums, and streaming offsets

Mina / Rishi — read Jordan's ask and Mina's reply. For Noble's short-chat heavy profile I suggest we propose a blended package:

- Commit structure: Monthly commit with a 3-month smoothing window (i.e., actual usage can be aggregated over the quarter for commit fulfillment). This avoids penalizing seasonality but preserves committed revenue.
- Floor / per-request: Offer a 25-token per-request floor for chat endpoints. That would simplify Noble's internal cost forecasts and is defensible given median prompt sizes.
- Rounding: Round streaming billable units up to the nearest 50 tokens. For non-streaming batch calls use per-token billing with a 1-token round-up.
- Carry-forward/true-up: Allow carry-forward credits up to 20% of the monthly commit within the quarter; any overage beyond commit + carry-forward billed at overage rate but eligible for higher-volume discount if they exceed the next tier.

I've drafted suggested contract language below to keep Legal happy (simple, limited definitions):

"Billable Token" means the sum of input and output tokens generated by the Service for a Customer request. Partial tokens are rounded up in accordance with the billing profile set forth in the Order Form.

"Streaming Offset" means a per-call fixed billable token amount applied to streaming sessions to account for connection overhead; subsequent tokens are billed in increments set forth in the Order Form.

These are intentionally short so our legal team can fold them into the SOW redline. Rishi, any thoughts on technical feasibility for per-call prefix + 50-token rounding?

-marissa
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on metering: rounding, minimums, and streaming offsets (draft wording)

Agree with Marissa's approach; technically feasible with current metering pipeline. Two tweaks to the definition I'd add before Legal signs off:

1) Clarify partial-token handling: meter emits fractional tokens internally but the billing pipeline applies rounding only at billing-window aggregation; for streaming offsets we apply prefix at session start and then aggregate fractional tokens into 50-token buckets for billing. This avoids per-frame charging noise.

2) Call out system tokens: include system/instruction tokens in the billable token definition so there is no ambiguity about assistant/system tokens the model emits.

Draft clause for SOW insertion (please copy/paste into redline):

"Billable Tokens: For purposes of invoicing, Billable Tokens are the sum of (i) input tokens, (ii) system/instruction tokens, and (iii) output tokens generated by the Service in response to a Customer request. Token usage is reported as a fractional value by the Service telemetry; invoicing shall round such usage in accordance with the Billing Profile specified in the Order Form. For Customers subscribed to a Streaming Profile, each streaming session shall incur a Streaming Offset (a fixed billable token amount) at session initiation; thereafter, token consumption shall be aggregated and billed in increments of the Rounding Increment set forth in the Order Form.

Billing Profile examples: Default: per-token rounding (round up to nearest token). Streaming Profile: 10-token prefix + 50-token rounding thereafter.

Let me know and I can reformat for Legal.

-rishi
Director, Sales Engineering

Subject: Re: Questions on metering: billable token floors, ceilings, and streaming offsets — proposed SOW language & next steps

Jordan — attached is a short redline (NR_commit_redline_20261114.pdf) and the token worksheet mapping your sample to the proposed structures. Summary of the proposed SOW terms:

- Commit: Monthly committed usage with a 3-month smoothing window (quarterly aggregation for commit fulfillment).
- Rounding & per-request floor: For chat endpoints, a 25-token per-request floor plus 50-token rounding on streaming consumption. Batch endpoints remain per-token billed with 1-token round-up.
- Streaming Offset: 10-token prefix applied at session start; subsequent tokens aggregated and billed in 50-token increments.
- Carry-forward / True-up: Up to 20% of monthly commit may carry forward within the quarter. Overage billed at agreed overage rate.
- Legal clause: included in the attached redline. We included the Billable Tokens and Streaming Offset definitions Rishi drafted.

Action items:
- Jordan / Procurement: confirm acceptance of the above billing profile so we can attach the SOW to your PO (we've prepared a DocuSign link for signature).
- Noble: if you prefer a per-session flat fee instead of prefix + rounding, say so and we'll price that variant.

DocuSign (ready for Noble): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerForm?powerFormId=abc123-nr-sign
